name: Prologis, Inc.

profile.description: Prologis, Inc. is the world's largest industrial REIT, owning, operating, and developing approximately 1.2 billion square feet of logistics and distribution facilities across 20 countries. The company serves ~6,700 customers including Amazon, FedEx, and DHL. Prologis is expanding into data center development with a 5.7-gigawatt power pipeline and operates the Prologis Essentials platform (solar, EV charging, LED lighting). As a REIT, it distributes at least 90% of taxable income. Founded in 1983, headquartered in San Francisco, California.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Prologis has meaningfully expanded beyond pure logistics landlording — the 5.7-gigawatt data center power pipeline represents a major new revenue vertical, and the Prologis Essentials platform (solar energy, EV charging, LED lighting, racking) monetizes real estate beyond rent [1][3]. Q1 2026 development starts of $1,783M (81.2% build-to-suit) reflect continued execution. These are significant extensions, though the core warehouse model remains fundamentally unchanged. AI Deployment (1/2): CTO described deploying AI internally to analyze data across 1.2B sq ft, optimize capital allocation, and automate operational workflows, but no externally-facing AI products ship to customers [3]. Market Share (2/2): Undisputed global leader in logistics real estate at ~1.2 billion sq ft — roughly 3x the next largest competitor — maintaining 95.3% occupancy with record Q1 2026 lease signings of 64 million square feet [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): $3,500-$4,500M development pipeline for 2026 with accelerating data center projects, but these are capital deployments rather than named next-gen products with specific launch timelines [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Prologis Ventures invests in logistics technology startups, and the company's technology platform for space planning and AI-enabled operations represents above-average innovation investment for the REIT sector [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Prologis's purpose — to be the foundation of global commerce, enabling the movement of goods that sustain modern life — is specific, thoughtful, and validated by 40+ years of consistent execution under founder Hamid Moghadam through multiple market cycles including the 2008 crisis and pandemic e-commerce surge [2]. The purpose clearly differentiates from REIT peers and connects logistics to a larger societal function. However, it describes what the company does exceptionally well rather than a bold future state that doesn't yet exist. Community Impact (1/2): The Community Workforce Initiative trains thousands of logistics workers annually in underserved communities, and Prologis holds 10 GRESB Green Stars with a net-zero 2040 commitment [4]. Dollar amounts for community investment were not specifically quantified. Employee Retention (1/2): CEO succession from 42-year founder Moghadam to 20-year veteran Dan Letter on January 1, 2026 demonstrates exceptional leadership retention [2]. The lean 2,802-person organization has been recognized on Fortune's Best Workplaces lists. However, Glassdoor reviews note centralized, top-down management. Insider Buying (0/2): Insider activity in 2025-2026 has been predominantly selling, with corporate insider ownership at only 0.52% and no significant net insider buying identified [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Q1 2026 delivered $2,298M revenue (up 7.4% YoY) with Core FFO of $1.50/share and record lease signings of 64M sq ft at 95.3% occupancy [1]. Management raised 2026 guidance to Core FFO of $6.07-$6.23/share with same-store NOI growth of 6.25-7.00% cash basis. D/E of 64.8% ($34.7B debt against $53.5B equity) is well within the 70% target, supported by A-rated balance sheet and $6.7B liquidity [1]. Profit margin of 36.6% significantly exceeds the 20% target. Five-year revenue CAGR of 14.2% is strong. Key drags: ROE of 6.84% (typical for equity-heavy REITs but well below 15% target), forward P/E of 43.0 reflecting premium valuation, and GAAP payout ratio of 112% (FFO-based payout is a healthier ~69% as expected for REITs). Strong dividend profile: 27 consecutive years paid, 13 consecutive years of growth, 11.2% 5-year dividend CAGR [5].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Prologis owns and operates physical logistics real estate — warehouses, distribution centers, and strategically located land — that AI structurally cannot substitute. AI actually amplifies demand for Prologis's assets: AI data centers require large-footprint, power-ready facilities that Prologis is uniquely positioned to develop through its 5.7-gigawatt pipeline, and AI-driven e-commerce growth increases distribution space requirements [1][3]. Management highlighted at the 2025 Groundbreakers conference that AI and energy reliability are primary demand drivers. Physical infrastructure, zoning, permitting, and construction represent irreplaceable capabilities beyond software's reach. While AI-driven supply chain optimization could modestly reduce per-unit space requirements, 95.3% occupancy and 31.9% net effective rent change in Q1 2026 show no evidence of demand erosion [1]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Prologis is actively developing data center infrastructure for AI and cloud computing through its 5.7-gigawatt power pipeline, representing quantifiable AI-related infrastructure revenue from a strategic new vertical [1].

infinite_game.summary: Prologis under founder Hamid Moghadam built a 42-year track record of consistent logistics real estate leadership, and the orderly succession to 20-year veteran Dan Letter on January 1, 2026 demonstrates institutional continuity [2]. The strategic expansion into data centers and energy services shows flexibility, and the REIT structure enforces patience through long-duration assets. However, the company's purpose remains more operational than inspirational — it excels at what it does rather than articulating a transformative vision of a future state. Sinek would recognize the long-term infrastructure mindset but note the lack of a truly galvanizing Just Cause beyond operational excellence.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Prologis has a genuine purpose — enabling global commerce through logistics infrastructure — validated by 42 years of Moghadam's leadership through multiple market crises including 2008, the pandemic, and trade disruptions [2]. Strategic decisions consistently trace to this purpose, and the company has maintained focus through industry cycles. However, 'being the foundation of global commerce' describes what the company does superbly, not a bold vision of a future state that doesn't yet exist. Sinek would call this a strong mission, not quite a Just Cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The CEO succession from Moghadam to Dan Letter (20-year veteran) was smooth and planned, and Prologis has been recognized on Fortune's Best Workplaces lists [2]. The lean 2,802-person organization managing $200B+ in assets requires high delegation and trust. However, Glassdoor reviews describe a 'highly centralized, crystal-clear strategy with an intense execution cadence' that limits bottom-up input, and some reviewers note top-down management styles that constrain organizational trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Prologis acknowledges competitors' strengths constructively. At the 2024 Groundbreakers conference, the CEO and FedEx Chairman discussed industry evolution rather than competitive destruction [3]. Management commentary focuses on improving logistics outcomes and serving customer needs rather than crushing specific REIT competitors. The data center expansion was motivated by serving hyperscaler demand, not attacking Digital Realty or Equinix.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The data center expansion and Prologis Essentials platform (solar, EV charging, energy storage) represent meaningful strategic evolution — leveraging existing land, power infrastructure, and development expertise for adjacent verticals [1]. However, this is incremental flexibility extending the core platform rather than a transformative reinvention. The logistics REIT model remains dominant, and Prologis is adding capabilities rather than abandoning a legacy business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Prologis committed to net-zero by 2040, continued development starts during the 2023-2024 demand softening, and committed early to data center land conversion when economics were uncertain [1][4]. These demonstrate willingness to invest for the long term. However, with a $130B+ market cap, A-rated balance sheet, $6.7B liquidity, and dominant market position, these bets carry limited relative risk — courage is easier when the financial cushion is this deep.

investment_thesis: Prologis delivered solid Q1 2026 results with $2,298M revenue (up 7.4% YoY), Core FFO of $1.50/share, and record lease signings of 64 million square feet at 95.3% occupancy [1]. Management raised 2026 guidance to Core FFO of $6.07-$6.23/share with same-store cash NOI growth of 6.25-7.00%. The 5.7-gigawatt data center power pipeline positions Prologis to capture AI infrastructure demand, while the core logistics franchise benefits from e-commerce growth, supply chain reshoring, and net effective rent changes of 31.9% that signal significant embedded growth as in-place rents roll to market [1]. The 3.1% dividend yield backed by 13 consecutive years of growth, 11.2% 5-year CAGR, and an A-rated balance sheet with $6.7B liquidity provides a reliable income profile for dividend investors [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on valuation — at 35.9x trailing earnings and forward P/E of ~43, Prologis is priced as a premium growth compounder despite 7.4% revenue growth [5]. ROE of 6.84% reflects the capital-intensive REIT model, and the GAAP payout ratio exceeds 100% (though FFO-based payout is a healthier ~69%). Industrial real estate faces cyclical risks from potential economic slowdown — occupancy peaked at 97.5% in 2022 and has normalized to 95.3%, and further softening could compress both rental rates and multiples [1]. The data center pivot enters a competitive market where specialized REITs (Equinix, Digital Realty) have deeper expertise. Rising interest rates would increase costs on $34.7B of debt (currently 3.3% weighted average) and compress REIT valuations broadly. The CEO transition from 42-year founder Moghadam to Dan Letter introduces execution uncertainty even with Letter's two decades of experience [2].
key_catalysts: Data center pipeline monetization: Converting the 5.7-gigawatt power pipeline into signed hyperscaler leases could add 10-20% to Core FFO and re-rate PLD toward infrastructure REIT multiples
Embedded rent growth realization: 31.9% net effective rent change on Q1 2026 renewals with in-place rents still 20-30% below market provides a multi-year organic NOI growth engine
Supply chain reshoring and nearshoring trends creating sustained demand for Class A logistics space in high-barrier, high-growth markets globally
key_risks: Premium valuation at 35.9x trailing P/E leaves minimal margin of safety — any deceleration in leasing velocity or occupancy normalization below 95% could trigger significant multiple compression
Rising interest rate environment would increase cost on $34.7B debt and compress REIT valuations broadly, while $6.7B liquidity provides only partial buffer against sustained rate pressure
Data center expansion enters a competitive market where Equinix, Digital Realty, and hyperscalers building their own facilities create leasing, pricing, and development cost uncertainties
